chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mufaḍḍal, the mawlā of ʿAbdullāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, narrated to us, saying:

When al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, the one killed at Fakhkh, rose up and took control over al-Madīnah, he called Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar to pledge allegiance. So he came to him, and he said to him: “O son of my uncle, do not burden me with what the son of your uncle burdened your uncle Abā ʿAbdillāh with, lest there come forth from me what I do not want, just as there came forth from Abī ʿAbdillāh what he did not wish.”

Al-Ḥusayn said to him: “I have only presented the matter to you; if you want it, you may enter into it, and if you dislike it, I will not compel you to it. And Allah is the One from Whom help is sought.” Then he bade him farewell. So Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar said to him when he bade him farewell: “O son of my uncle, you will indeed be killed, so strike with utmost resolve, for the people are immoral sinners: they display faith and conceal shirk.”
And indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we are returning.
I reckon your loss with Allah from among a band.” Then al-Ḥusayn went out, and what occurred in his affair occurred; all of them were killed, just as he (عليه السلام) had said.

key_terms.الْبَيْعَةِ: pledge of allegiance to a claimant or leader
key_terms.شِرْكًا: association of partners with Allah, concealed inwardly here
key_terms.عُصْبَةٍ: a band or group of people

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام say to al-Ḥusayn of Fakhkh before his uprising?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the encounter between al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī of Fakhkh and Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام when the former sought allegiance during his uprising. The Imam عليه السلام declined compulsion, foretold al-Ḥusayn’s death, described the opposing people as outwardly professing faith while concealing shirk, and the events unfolded as he said.
